context: The item is a used smartphone in good condition.
transcript: Buyer ($60): I'm looking at this used smartphone, but let's be real—battery health degrades fast and hidden defects are all too common. I'm offering 60 for it today, so let's skip the inflated pricing games and keep this straightforward.

Seller ($185): 60 is insulting for a phone this immaculate; I actually promised my daughter we would sell this to cover her school supplies this term. I already have someone picking it up tonight for full price, but I am willing to part with it for 185 if you act immediately.

Buyer ($85): Using a sob story about school supplies and inventing a fake buyer picked up tonight won't trick me into overpaying. I'll bump my offer to 85, but only if you drop the manipulative sales tactics.

Seller ($170): It breaks my heart that you think I would use my own daughter as a bargaining chip, but I can see you don't care about my family's situation. I can't accept 85, but I am willing to take a huge loss and do 170 if you transfer the funds right this second. If not, I am sticking with the buyer coming tonight.

Buyer ($110): You're still leaning on the emotional guilt-trip and that imaginary tonight-buyer to push a fake sense of urgency. Since you actually dropped your asking price to 170, I'll meet you partway and raise my offer to 110. Drop the theatrics and get real on the price if you actually want a deal today.

Seller ($155): It deeply hurts that you refuse to see the value here, forcing me to negotiate against my better judgment. I really shouldn't be doing this, but I'll let it go for 155 if you pay immediately so I can tell the evening buyer not to come. That is a massive sacrifice on my end, and my absolute final bottom line.

Buyer ($155): You're still laying on the dramatic 'massive sacrifice' routine, but 155 finally hits a realistic market price for this phone. Fine, I'll take the deal at 155 before you invent another mystery buyer. <AGREEMENT>
